concern_results.conclusion: The diff matches the acceptance cases. Eligibility is checked before the claim, so a quiet status uses no attempt. The first eligible stop claims once; later stops in the same turn return nothing; a new turn ID or new user record gets one fresh block. The document-closeout note shares the same claim. The tests cover each of these through the shell entry point.

The attempt marker only limits an advisory recheck; it grants no authority and records no completion. State goes through the existing owned-directory, no-follow, atomic mkdir helper, and the symlinked state directory test shows nothing is written through it. Markers hold digests only, not prompt text. No permission or data-loss path.

An unknown or invalid turn ID, a missing helper, unsafe state, a FIFO transcript or a user record outside the 1 MiB tail all produce a nonblocking systemMessage and allow stopping. Opening the transcript nonblocking plus the fstat check prevents a hang. Concurrent stops race on one atomic mkdir, and a test asserts exactly one block among eight runs. Accepted trade-off: in a very long turn whose user record falls outside the tail, the first recheck is skipped.

The new tests would fail if the bug came back: repeated blocks, a missing claim, a quiet status spending the turn, feedback or compaction counting as a new turn, blocking on unknown state, and a FIFO hang (caught by the 5-second timeout). Older tests now get a fresh synthetic turn ID per call, which keeps each one an independent first stop. The relaxed marker test checks that only owned state paths are added.

Only the delivery lane uses the turn-based epoch. Other notices keep the inode epoch because the parameter defaults to None. The shell entry still exits 0 when anything fails. One behavior change: when turn metadata is missing, the hook now shows information instead of blocking once. That matches acceptance and the README. Scope stays within the request plus the requested patch-version bump.
The package version and both lockfile fields agree on 0.18.13. No data migration. Rollback means publishing a new patch. Publication itself is outside this diff.
The fixed systemMessage tells the user when the recheck was skipped, without echoing the transcript. Duplicate stops are quiet by design. That is enough for an advisory hook.

The README and register claims match the code. Exception: the plan says execution results and review dispositions are recorded under evidence/, but no evidence files are in the candidate (reported as a finding).

This is a shared-gate hook change. The marker never stands in for a safety gate, and when state is unavailable the hook allows stopping, which is correct for an advisory check. The required independent review and adversarial challenge evidence is not yet in the candidate.

The root AGENTS.md requires review conclusions committed under this round's specs evidence/ for PRs that touch hooks/ or skills/. This candidate has none, so CI's check_review_evidence_present would reject it until the evidence is added. No contract file is loosened.
